newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia overnight hits low of 5.5/7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia overnight hits low of 5.5/7 pct.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate hit a low of 5.5 percent against 6.0 percent previously as banks lent short-term in anticipation of withdrawals for two festivals next month, dealers said on Wednesday.
They said this was the lowest level for the overnight rate in many months, below the central banks's perceived floor of 5.8/6.0 percent.
At 0820 GMT, the overnight money was trading at 5.7 percent.
Dealers said banks were expecting withdrawals to increase substantially in the next few days as the Moslem Eid al-Fitr and Chinese Lunar New Year festivals draw near.
"This is the lowest level for the overnight rate recently. It usually attracts central bank intervention," a dealer with a Malaysian bank said.
He said it was possible that Bank Negara was viewing the situation as a temporary aberration and may not intervene.
Dealers said banks had made heavy cash withdrawals to enable their depositors to withdraw cash for the festivals. This has reduced liquidity for longer tenors and pushed up other rates.
An estimated two billion ringgit to three billion ringgit are expected to leave the banking system temporarily in the form of cash for the twin celebrations, the dealers said.
They said a few large local banks, which held excess funds, were also mainly lending in the overnight market in the hope of longer-term rates rising further ahead of the festivals.
However, other dealers said the big banks were probably under the directive of the central bank to keep the liquidity out of the system to maintain its high interest-rate policy.
No confirmation was available from Bank Negara, which does not comment on its market intervention operations.
